overview: In the middle of Tintagel village stands the Old Post Office, a stone house from the 1300s laid out like a little medieval manor, with a cottage garden around it. It got its name in Victorian times, when it briefly served as the area’s letter-receiving office, and has been restored to look as it did then.

It was one of the National Trust’s very first properties, bought in 1903 after a local woman and a group of artists raised money to save it from demolition. It’s a small, quick visit and a lovely contrast to the castle down the road.

expect.title: The house
expect.text: A Grade I listed medieval house laid out like a manor in miniature, with the Victorian post office restored inside.

expect.title: The garden
expect.text: A cottage garden surrounds the house.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: It closes over the winter months; check the National Trust website for dates.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry for non-members; National Trust members get in free.

week.text: A quick, charming stop to add to a Tintagel day, either before or after the castle.

pairWith.why: the legendary castle a short walk down the lane
a small museum on the same street
a sandy cove a short drive away

tips: Pop in on your way to or from the castle: it’s in the village, a short walk away.

setting.note: A small historic house and cottage garden
